Byomkesh.description: The central detective figure, known as a 'satyanweshi' or truth-seeker, who investigates mysteries with keen observation and logic.

Ajit.description: Byomkesh's close friend and chronicler, who narrates their adventures and assists in investigations.

Satyabati.description: Byomkesh's wife, who shares a close familial bond with Ajit and is expecting a child during this chapter.

Rajarama.description: An elderly descendant of Janakirama and head of the family during the time of the Sepoy Mutiny; father of Jayarama.

Jayarama.description: Rajarama's son, a youth who assists his father in trying to protect their family fortune.

Ram Binod.description: A descendant of Janakirama, elder brother of Ram Kishore Singh, who dies young under mysterious circumstances.

Ram Kishore Singh.description: Younger brother of Ram Binod, who rebuilds the family fortune, repurchases the ancestral estate, and becomes the patriarch.

Banshidhar.description: Ram Kishore's eldest son, known for his fierce temper and involvement in managing the zamindari.

Muralidhar.description: Ram Kishore's second son, physically disabled and sly, rumored to have committed crimes with his servant Ganpat.

Haripriya.description: Ram Kishore's daughter, envious and sharp-tongued, whose marriage to Monilal ends with her mysterious death by snakebite.

Monilal.description: Haripriya's husband, a calm and educated man who becomes a 'ghar-jamai' living with his wife's family.

Gadadhar.description: Ram Kishore's simple-minded teenage son, more interested in roaming the woods than in studies.

Tulsi.description: Ram Kishore's youngest daughter, sharp-eyed, restless, and sensible, but traumatized by witnessing Haripriya's death.

Ganpat.description: Muralidhar's loyal and wicked servant, rumored to assist his master in various misdeeds.

Chandmohan Dutta.description: The family's long-serving steward, shrewd and knowledgeable about property and estate affairs.

Ramapati.description: A distant relative given shelter by Ram Kishore, intended as a tutor for the younger children but largely ignored.

Bulaki Lal.description: Ram Kishore's old chauffeur, responsible for the family's motor car and known for preparing bhang thandai.

Ishanchandra Majumdar.description: A retired professor and old family friend, whose mysterious death by snakebite becomes the focus of the investigation.

Purandar Pandey.description: The local D.S.P. (Deputy Superintendent of Police), a friend of Byomkesh, who invites him to investigate the case.

Dr. Ghatak.description: The resident physician for Ram Kishore's family, involved in the aftermath of the mysterious deaths.

Sadhu.description: A holy man who sets up camp near the well and becomes a mysterious presence in the story.

Company rule.description: Refers to the period of British East India Company administration in India before direct Crown rule.

Janakirama.description: The original founder of the family lineage whose descendants are central to the story.

zamindari.description: A system of landholding and revenue collection in colonial India, with zamindars as landlords.

Sepoy Mutiny.description: The Indian Rebellion of 1857, a major uprising against British rule.

Santhal.description: An indigenous tribal group in eastern India; here, refers to a Santhal village near the fort.

Bengal.description: A region in eastern India, historically significant and culturally rich.

ghee.description: Clarified butter used in Indian cooking and rituals.

Berhampore College.description: A college in Berhampore, a city in West Bengal.

B.Sc..description: Bachelor of Science degree, an undergraduate academic degree.

ghar-jamai.description: A son-in-law who lives with his wife's family, often considered a dependent.

Vaishnav.description: A follower of Vaishnavism, a major tradition within Hinduism devoted to Vishnu.

Bedes.description: A nomadic tribe in Bengal, known as snake charmers and performers.

shilajit.description: A mineral-rich substance used in traditional Indian medicine.

Santal Parganas.description: A region in present-day Jharkhand, India, historically inhabited by the Santal tribe.

Harrison Road.description: A major thoroughfare in Calcutta (now Kolkata), where Byomkesh resides.

Nepal.description: A neighboring country to India, mentioned as the residence of Professor Majumdar's son-in-law.

Genghis Khan.description: The Mongol conqueror, referenced metaphorically to describe Banshidhar's brutality.

Yama.description: The Hindu god of death, used to describe Ramkishore's fearsome authority.

Bihar.description: An Indian state neighboring Bengal, referenced in relation to old house architecture.

Badshahs.description: Refers to Mughal emperors; here, indicates the era of the gold mohur coin.

mohar.description: A gold coin used in India during the Mughal era.

asharfi.description: A gold coin, similar to the mohar, used in historical India.

krosh.description: An ancient Indian unit of distance, roughly 2-3 miles.

dhoti.description: A traditional men's garment, a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

bhang.description: An intoxicating drink made from cannabis leaves, consumed especially during festivals.

bhang thandai.description: A cold, sweet beverage flavored with bhang (cannabis), milk, and spices.

sal.description: A type of hardwood tree native to India, valued for timber.

satyanweshi.description: A seeker of truth; Byomkesh's self-description as a detective.

didi.description: A respectful term for elder sister in Bengali and Hindi.

baba.description: A term of respect for an elder or holy man; also used for fathers.

Mahashay.description: A respectful Bengali term for 'gentleman' or 'sir.'

cubits.description: An ancient unit of length, roughly the length of a forearm (about 18 inches).

bighas.description: A traditional unit of land measurement in India, varying regionally but generally about 1/3 acre.

para.description: A neighborhood or locality, especially in Bengali context.
